title: Order of operations
blurb: Evaluate any expression in the agreed order: grouping, exponents, then multiplication and division and addition and subtraction, left to right where ranks tie.
question: A classmate says 20 − 12 ÷ 4 × 2 equals 18.5, and a basic calculator shows 4. What is the correct value, and which rule did each of them break?

teach.body: Formally, the order of operations is the convention for evaluating an expression: grouping symbols first, then exponents and roots, then multiplication and division from left to right, then addition and subtraction from left to right. In plain English: everyone works an expression in the same order so everyone gets the same answer. On the HESI A2, each wrong option is usually the value you get by doing one step out of order.

Multiplication and division share one rank, and so do addition and subtraction. Within a rank, work strictly left to right. So 8 ÷ 2 × 4 = 4 × 4 = 16, not 8 ÷ 8 = 1, and 10 − 3 + 2 = 9, not 10 − 5 = 5. The letters in PEMDAS list M before D and A before S only because a word needs an order; they are not a ranking.

teach.h: Left to right vs the classic slip
teach.caption: The slip column is what a candidate gets by multiplying first, adding first, or working straight across.

items: 20 − 12 ÷ 4 × 2: divide first (it is on the left), 12 ÷ 4 = 3; then 3 × 2 = 6; then 20 − 6 = 14.
Check: doing 4 × 2 first gives 20 − 1.5 = 18.5, and working straight across gives 4. Both are wrong.
A number touching parentheses means multiply: 2(16) = 32.

teach.text: −3² = −(3²) = −9, but (−3)² = 9: the exponent applies before the negative sign unless the sign is inside parentheses. And never multiply before a division that sits to its left: 24 ÷ 4 × 2 is 12, not 3.

teach.body: Destiny Clark, a nursing applicant volunteering at a clinic, receives 4 boxes of 50 gauze pads and 3 boxes of 25, then uses 60. She writes 4 × 50 + 3 × 25 − 60. Multiply first: 200 + 75 − 60. Then left to right: 275 − 60 = 215 pads. Working straight across instead, (4 × 50 + 3) × 25 − 60, would give 5,015, far more pads than she received.

items: Order: grouping, exponents and roots, × and ÷ left to right, + and − left to right.
× and ÷ are equal in rank; so are + and −. Ties go left to right.
A fraction bar and brackets group like parentheses; work the innermost group first.
Enter one step at a time on a basic calculator.

summary: You can now evaluate expressions in the correct order of operations, working left to right where ranks tie and treating brackets and fraction bars as grouping. You can also name the out-of-order step behind each wrong value a HESI A2 option offers.

A.why: Exponent first: 3² = 9. Then ÷ and × left to right: 24 ÷ 4 = 6, 6 × 2 = 12. Then add: 12 + 9 = 21.

whyNot.0: 12 multiplies 4 × 2 before dividing: 24 ÷ 8 + 9 = 12. Division comes first because it is on the left.
whyNot.2: 225 works left to right and squares the whole result: (12 + 3)² = 15².

A.why: Multiply first: 3 × 4 = 12. Then add and subtract left to right: 50 − 20 = 30; 30 + 5 = 35; 35 − 12 = 23.

whyNot.0: 13 adds 20 + 5 before subtracting from 50; addition does not outrank subtraction.
whyNot.1: 128 works strictly left to right, multiplying last: (50 − 20 + 5 − 3) × 4.
whyNot.3: 37 subtracts the group 20 + 5 − 12 from 50 as if it were in parentheses.

A.why: Parentheses: 15 − 3 = 12 and 2 + 4 = 6. Then left to right: 12 ÷ 6 = 2, and 2 × 5 = 10.

whyNot.1: 0.4 multiplies 6 × 5 before dividing: 12 ÷ 30. Division is on the left, so it goes first.

B.q: A student types 6 + 18 ÷ 3 × 2 − 4 into a basic calculator one key at a time and gets 12. What is the correct value?
B.why: Divide and multiply first, left to right: 18 ÷ 3 = 6, 6 × 2 = 12. Then 6 + 12 − 4 = 14.

whyNot.2: 12 is the calculator's left-to-right result, (6 + 18) ÷ 3 × 2 − 4, which skips the order of operations.

whyNot.0: 3 subtracts 10 − 4 first: 6 × 4 ÷ 8. Multiplication comes before subtraction.
whyNot.1: 12 squares −2 as −4, giving 4 × (−4) ÷ 8 = −2 and 10 − (−2) = 12; a negative squared is positive.
whyNot.2: 14 squares the 3 before working the parentheses: 1 − 9 = −8, so 10 − (−4) = 14.

B.why: Parentheses: 5 + 4 = 9. Then left to right: 6 × 9 = 54 and 54 ÷ 3 = 18. Finally 3 + 18 − 7 = 14.

whyNot.1: 12 doubles 3 instead of squaring it: 18 − 6 = 12, then 24 ÷ 3 + 4.

C.q: An IV bag holds 1,000 mL. It infuses 125 mL per hour for 4 hours, then 2 doses of 50 mL each are added to the bag. How many milliliters are in the bag?
C.why: The amount is 1,000 − 125 × 4 + 2 × 50. Multiply first: 1,000 − 500 + 100. Then left to right: 500 + 100 = 600 mL.

whyNot.0: 400 mL subtracts the added doses as well: 1,000 − (500 + 100).
whyNot.2: 500 mL stops after the infusion and leaves out the 100 mL added.
whyNot.3: 550 mL adds only one 50 mL dose instead of 2 × 50.

whyNot.0: −12 gives −2 × (−5) a negative sign (−10 − 2); two negatives multiply to a positive.

reteach.title: The checkout lines
reteach.question: A store has an express lane, then two regular lines where customers are served in the order they arrived. How does that store explain the order of operations?

blocks.h: Lanes by rank, then first come, first served
blocks.body: Grouping symbols are the express lane: whatever is inside is served first. Exponents and roots come next. Then the multiply-and-divide line: × and ÷ customers stand in one line and are served in the order they arrived, which is left to right. Last is the add-and-subtract line, again served left to right. Nobody cuts in line just because their letter comes first in PEMDAS.

items: Served in arrival order, the answer is 11. ✓

blocks.text: A basic calculator serves every customer in one line as they arrive. Enter one step at a time so the × and ÷ line goes before the + and − line.

explain.body: Work inside parentheses, brackets and fraction bars before anything else, innermost first. Then square the whole group, not its parts.

whyNot.3: 170 squares each number inside the parentheses: 4 × (81 − 36) − 10.

explain.body: An exponent belongs only to the number (or group) it touches. Square that number before multiplying or dividing anything.

test.why: Exponent: 5² = 25. Then left to right: 2 × 25 = 50 and 50 ÷ 10 = 5.

explain.body: Multiplication and division have equal rank. In 40 ÷ 5 × 2 − 6, the division comes first because it is on the left.

test.why: Left to right for ÷ and ×: 40 ÷ 5 = 8, 8 × 2 = 16. Then 16 − 6 = 10.

whyNot.0: −2 multiplies 5 × 2 first: 40 ÷ 10 − 6. Division is on the left, so it comes first.

explain.body: Addition does not outrank subtraction. Work them in the order they appear: 30 − 12 + 8 means 18 + 8, not 30 − 20.

whyNot.2: 16 subtracts the whole group 12 + 8 − 6 = 14 from 30 as if it were in parentheses.
whyNot.3: 32 adds the 6 instead of subtracting it: 18 + 8 + 6.
